text:
ConocoPhillips dropped 3.1% today as crude oil prices fell sharply on growing hopes for U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks. Oil declined to session lows as news broke of ongoing peace negotiations, with the U.S. and Iran both reportedly pursuing diplomacy to ease Mideast tensions rather than escalating military conflict. For an oil company, lower crude prices directly pressure profitability—even though the stock is up 2.7% over the past two weeks, today's retreat wiped out those gains and more.

The broader context is the market's uncertainty about oil supply and geopolitical risk. Earlier this month, tensions spiked enough to push the stock up sharply (it closed near $154 on October 30), but as diplomatic signals improve, traders are repricing that risk downward. Oil companies thrive on uncertainty and supply concerns; the moment those ease, the tailwind reverses.
